Subject: MAP kickoff & procurement window — Sierra Diagnostics

Hi Michael / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to document a clear mutual action plan so they can align internal stakeholders (legal, security, and finance) against a target decision window the week of July 20. Attached is our internal timeline (Sierra_Timeline_v1.xlsx) and a short list of must-have evidence items: SOC 2 summary, a completed security questionnaire, and a signed MSA + DPA before purchase order can be raised.

Can you confirm Redwood's expected sequencing for MSA / DPA / Order Form? Our procurement team prefers: security evidence -> DPA review -> signature of MSA + Order Form together via DocuSign, but they can be flexible if there are gating constraints.

We also flagged two quick questions for legal: 1) any non-standard indemnity language we should expect, and 2) whether Redwood requires subprocessor disclosure earlier in the process.

Appreciate a succinct MAP so we can lock July 20 as the target.

Thanks,
Samantha Riggs

Samantha — thanks for the timeline and clarity. Putting a concise MAP below and copying legal and sales ops to confirm sequencing. High level (proposed):

- Week of Jun 22: Redwood provides SOC 2 summary + completed security questionnaire draft (we'll attach SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf and security_questionnaire_sierra.xlsx).
- Jun 24–26: Legal (Redwood) reviews MSA draft; we will flag any non-standard clauses early.
- Jun 29: DPA comments exchanged in parallel with MSA review (DPA should be lightweight — we can provide standard language).
- Jul 6: Finalized MSA + DPA ready for signature; Order Form prepared with pricing and initial usage caps.
- Jul 7–9: DocuSign window for signature (MSA+DPA+Order Form).
- Jul 20: Procurement target for PO/commitment — we leave buffer for any last-minute procurement approvals.

Open items and assumptions:
- If Sierra requires custom indemnity language, this will likely add 5–7 business days (needs early flag).
- Subprocessor list: we can provide a current snapshot immediately; full quarterly disclosure is part of our standard ops.
- If you need the MSA redlines sooner, we can push an initial draft by EOD Jun 23.

Laura / Karthik / Kimberly — can you confirm the sequencing above from legal + security perspective and call out any gating items that would force the signatures to separate (e.g., DPA approval after MSA sign)?

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of GTM Integrations | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 22, 2026 at 10:03 AM michael_grant@redwood.ai wrote:
> Michael proposed a target sequencing. See below — legal confirmation follows.

Team / Samantha — quick legal notes:

1) Preferred sequencing: we will aim to deliver the MSA redline and DPA concurrently. Our legal team recommends signing MSA + DPA together in DocuSign to avoid duplicate signature cycles. Order Form can be packaged into the same envelope as long as commercial terms are fully agreed.

2) Gating items to watch:
  - Indemnity / liability caps: if Sierra requests material changes, that will push the close by 1–2 weeks (needs executive approval).
  - Data residency clauses: if Sierra needs a strict EU/EAA residency clause, we need to loop infra (Marcus) for feasibility — that may extend timeline.
  - Subprocessors: we can provide the current list now; any concerns from Sierra would be handled via the DPA appendix.

3) Evidence: SOC2 summary is sufficient initially for procurement review; our SOC2 full report is on request under an NDA. We will attach the SOC2 summary now.

Action items for Redwood:
- Laura to send MSA redline (MSA_Redwood_draft_v0.9.docx) by Jun 24.
- Karthik to prepare a short legal exceptions matrix for quick exec review if there are material indemnity asks.
- Marcus to confirm there are no infra blockers for data residency (if raised).

Samantha — if procurement needs us to separate signatures (DPA after MSA), confirm and we'll schedule accordingly, but signing together is our recommended path.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Laura / Michael — this sequencing looks workable. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 

- SOC2 summary is fine for now; procurement has requested the full SOC2 report under NDA if we move to PO stage. We'll sign the NDA once redlines are mostly agreed.
- We prefer MSA + DPA + Order Form in one DocuSign envelope — simpler for our execs.
- Procurement noted two potential blockers that could delay to late July if surfaced: 1) any bespoke indemnity beyond standard market language, and 2) a requirement for strict data residency. Neither is expected today, but we wanted these called out so the MAP reflects them.

Can you confirm when the DocuSign envelope will be created and who will be the signers? Procurement prefers the envelope to be sent with an initial signing window of one week.

Thanks,
Samantha
